topic: Light is slow: the speed of light feels instant until you leave Earth - sunlight is 8 minutes old, Neptune's light is 4 hours old, Voyager 1 is 23 light-hours away, the nearest star is 4.24 light-years, and the observable universe is 93 billion light-years across - what cosmic distance really means
moral: The universe is not far away in space - it is far away in time, and every look at the sky is a look into the past

topic: The split-brain experiments: Sperry and Gazzaniga cut the corpus callosum and found two minds in one head - the left-hemisphere interpreter that invents reasons for what you do
moral: The 'you' that explains your choices is a story the left hemisphere tells - and the story is never the whole mind

topic: Betelgeuse: the red supergiant that dimmed, the dust cloud of 2019, and the supernova that will light our sky - 640 light-years of waiting
moral: The universe can rewrite the night sky overnight, so wonder is the only sane response to a sky we think we know

topic: The spotlight effect and the illusion of transparency: Gilovich's 2000 Barry Manilow shirt study and why nobody notices your embarrassment as much as you do
moral: Nobody is watching you as closely as you think - which is both a relief and a responsibility

topic: The binding problem: how 86 billion neurons produce one unified 'I' - binocular rivalry, gamma synchrony, and Crick and Koch's search for the neural correlate of consciousness
moral: Unity is not given to us - it is assembled moment by moment, which makes the self an achievement rather than a thing

topic: The Hubble tension: Planck says the universe expands at 67.4 km/s/Mpc, SH0ES says 73 - two trustworthy measurements that disagree and what it means for cosmology
moral: Two trustworthy measurements that disagree are not a failure of science - they are science showing us where the next discovery lives

topic: The bystander effect: Darley and Latane's 1968 smoke-filled room, diffusion of responsibility, and the real story behind the Kitty Genovese '37 witnesses' myth
moral: The crowd does not make us cruel - it makes us unsure, and one clear voice is enough to break the spell

topic: Libet's free will experiments: the readiness potential fires 300 milliseconds before you feel the decision - Soon's 2008 study, Schurger's 2012 critique, and what free will can still mean
moral: Free will may not be a spark before action but a veto, an attention and a responsibility we practise

topic: White dwarfs and the Chandrasekhar limit: the 1.4 solar-mass line that decides between a quiet death and a Type Ia supernova - and what happens to our Sun in five billion years
moral: Even a dead star can light the way - endings are often the most useful things in the universe

topic: Prospect theory: Kahneman and Tversky's 1979 proof that losses hurt about twice as much as gains feel good - loss aversion, the endowment effect, and the fear inside every decision
moral: We are not wired to be happy - we are wired not to lose, and every good decision starts with noticing that fear

topic: Anesthesia and consciousness: how propofol switches the mind off through GABA, the 1846 ether demonstration, burst suppression on the EEG, and the rare patients who wake up during surgery
moral: Consciousness is not a switch we understand - it is a process we borrow, and its fragility is what makes every waking hour a gift

topic: Gravitational waves: LIGO's GW150914 on 14 September 2015, two black holes merging 1.3 billion light-years away, three solar masses turned into ripples, and the 2017 Nobel Prize
moral: The universe has a soundtrack, and it took a century of patience to hear it

topic: The peak-end rule: Kahneman's 1993 cold-water experiment, the 2003 colonoscopy study, and why your memory judges an experience by its most intense moment and how it ended
moral: We do not remember our lives - we remember their peaks and their endings, so be careful how you end things

topic: Phantom limbs: Ramachandran's 1996 mirror box, cortical remapping after amputation, and why the brain keeps feeling a hand that is no longer there
moral: The body is a map the brain keeps drawing - and the map can be redrawn

topic: The first photograph of a black hole: the Event Horizon Telescope's 2019 image of M87*, 6.5 billion solar masses 55 million light-years away, eight telescopes and Katie Bouman's algorithm
moral: Humanity photographed the unphotographable by agreeing to look together - that is what civilisation is for

topic: Dopamine is not pleasure: Wolfram Schultz's reward prediction error, 'wanting' versus 'liking', and why the chase for more never satisfies
moral: Dopamine is not happiness - it is the pull toward more, and knowing that is how you stop being pulled

topic: The default mode network and the narrative self: Killingsworth and Gilbert's finding that the mind wanders 46.9% of waking life, and Metzinger's case that the self is a model, not a thing
moral: The self is a story told mostly when nothing else is happening - and you are allowed to edit the story

topic: Fast radio bursts: the Lorimer burst of 2007, CHIME's detection of a magnetar in 2020, and how a thousandth-of-a-second flash can outshine a galaxy
moral: Some of the loudest messages in the universe last a thousandth of a second - attention matters more than time

topic: Loneliness as a biological signal: John Cacioppo's work, Holt-Lunstad's 2015 meta-analysis of 26% higher mortality, inflammation, and why the pain of isolation is a hunger that wants an answer
moral: Loneliness is not weakness - it is a signal, and signals are meant to be answered

topic: Psychedelics and the ego: psilocybin, the 5-HT2A receptor, Carhart-Harris's 2012 finding that the default mode network quietens, and Johns Hopkins' 2020 depression trial
moral: The ego is a useful servant and a dangerous master - sometimes it takes a chemist to show you the door

topic: Titan: Cassini-Huygens landing in 2005, methane lakes at minus 179 Celsius, a thick nitrogen sky, and NASA's Dragonfly rotorcraft that will fly there
moral: Another world can be alien and familiar at once - that is what makes it worth going to

topic: The habit loop: how the basal ganglia turn a choice into an automatic routine - Ann Graybiel's MIT work, cue-routine-reward, and the 66-day myth of habit formation
moral: You are not your intentions - you are your repetitions, so choose them deliberately

topic: The hard problem versus illusionism: Chalmers' 1995 question, Dennett's reply, philosophical zombies, and Mary's room - is experience the deepest fact or the most convincing illusion?
moral: Either experience is the deepest fact in the universe or the most convincing illusion - either way it is the only thing any of us has ever directly known

topic: The Wow! signal: 15 August 1977, Ohio State's Big Ear telescope, 72 seconds at the 1420 MHz hydrogen line, and why it never came back
moral: One unrepeated signal is a question, not an answer - honest wonder is better than a false conclusion

topic: The placebo effect: Beecher's 1955 paper, sham knee surgery in 2002, Kaptchuk's open-label placebo trials, and why belief can change the body
moral: Belief is not magic, but it is chemistry - the mind is part of the treatment

topic: Near-death experiences: the Greyson scale, the Pam Reynolds case of 1991, oxygen and DMT hypotheses, and the AWARE study of 2014
moral: What people see at the edge of death tells us less about an afterlife than about the brain's last act of meaning-making

topic: Pluto and New Horizons: Clyde Tombaugh's 1930 discovery, the 14 July 2015 flyby, Sputnik Planitia's nitrogen glaciers, and what the 2006 reclassification really changed
moral: A demotion is not a disappearance - Pluto became more interesting the moment we finally saw it up close

topic: Procrastination is not laziness: Pychyl and Sirois on emotion regulation, present bias, and the implementation-intention technique that actually gets things started
moral: Procrastination is not a time problem - it is a feeling problem, and the way through it is one small honest step

topic: Henry Molaison and the memory that could not stay: the 1953 hippocampus surgery, mirror-tracing without remembering, and what HM taught us about who we are
moral: You are not your memories, but without them you cannot become anyone new

topic: The Hubble Deep Field: 342 exposures over ten days on an 'empty' patch of sky, thousands of galaxies in a speck, and the JWST deep fields that went further
moral: Point at the emptiest patch of sky and the universe answers with thousands of galaxies - emptiness is a failure of our attention

topic: Attachment theory: Bowlby and Ainsworth's 1970 strange situation, secure, anxious and avoidant patterns, and Hazan and Shaver's 1987 work on love as attachment
moral: How you were held as a child becomes how you hold others - but patterns learned can be learned again
